lead.headline: Nothing to change: the lineup is the projection lineup
lead.deck: Taylor and Downs are under way in London with Keenan Allen and Slayton inactive. Coker is unlikely to play tonight, which helps Waller. Re-check each starter 90 minutes before his kickoff.
lead.body: The bad news is the standing kind. Ollie Gordon, the back the priority claim was spent on, is on the bench for the first of the four weeks that count, in a backfield Miami say they will split, and the Ravens D/ST play without Trey Hendrickson. Overnight, the news ran the other way. Keenan Allen and Darius Slayton are both inactive in London, so Josh Downs, in the flex, is the Colts' lead receiver against the defence allowing the most points to receivers; ESPN's 13.6 for him hasn't moved, so that is upside the number hasn't counted. Adam Schefter reported this morning that Carolina's Jalen Coker is unlikely to play tonight. Darren Waller's one productive game came after Coker left, and ESPN lifted him from 9.3 to 10.1; he faces a Detroit defence that has given tight ends 100.1 points in three games. The free Mark Andrews is now exactly level with him, a coin flip on a seat that changed hands yesterday, so it stays. Everything else is as it was: no starter carries a designation, Saquon Barkley is off the report with DeVonta Smith now expected to miss two or three more games, and Rashee Rice was a full participant all week. This is the run before the inactive lists, so check each starter 90 minutes before his kickoff. Team 13 still start two players who are ruled out, which is why ESPN has you at 69%; that shrinks the moment they set a lineup.
